correctness.rationale: For a nontrivial primitive-four orbit, connectedness forces a common number of fires per four steps; nonclumpiness excludes twice per four because alternating firing forces two-step return. The only one-fire case has opposite left-side firing phases: the right-side threshold transition forces initial chips 0/1, and left-side inequalities give alpha in [b,b+r-1], beta in [r,b-1], 1<=r<=b-1. There are four phases, binom(b,r) labelled right choices, and r(b-r) left initial choices; their exact mass is 2b+i+j. Jiang confinement and complement produce all three-fire states and preserve primitivity. Binomial expansion proves the displayed exact polynomial and its endpoints. Two independent exhaustive dynamical enumerations match every coefficient in their tested ranges, and a separate integer polynomial checker validates identities to b=50. Finite tests do not serve as all-b proof.

value.rationale: Energy-resolved counts of primitive periodic states describe exact activity layers, not merely possible periods. K_{2,b} is the thinnest complete-bipartite infinite family permitting a primitive four-cycle. The theorem proves the precise support, all coefficients, and the sharp attainability and multiplicities at both strict middle-stair endpoints, which are motivated by prior optimal open-interval stability bounds. It also gives the explicit exponential total 2^(b+1)b(b-1). A family-wide classification and sharp natural boundary facts are substantial independently of any broader downstream theorem.
